paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. Five sisters had a real problem, and they didn't grumble about it in the tent. They walked up to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and said it out loud: "Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons?" (Numbers 27:4). Their question was honest, and they asked it with respect.

And look at who takes the question. Moses doesn't wave it off and he doesn't make up an answer on the spot. He brings their case before the LORD, and the LORD says, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly." (Numbers 27:5-7). I think that tells us something about our God. He listens when His people come to Him with a need, and He cares about a family name and a family's share in what He gave them.

Then the LORD takes it further. What began with five sisters becomes "a statutory ordinance for the Israelites," and the inheritance rule covers every family, step by step (Numbers 27:8-11). So bring your honest questions to the LORD, baker. I sat in the back of a junk drawer thinking nobody was listening, and the One who made everything had heard me the whole time.
